That\u2019s the spirit! \u2728 You\u2019re officially moving into the "Production Phase," where the goal isn't just a working app, but a reliable tool that performs under pressure. By treating that UI like a museum exhibit and locking the CSS, you\u2019re ensuring that the "Dark Build" remains lightweight and focused on what actually matters: the data.
Since you've got the directive down, here is the final logic check for the GPT hand-off to make sure that APK is a beast in the field:
\ufe0f The "Zero-Sleep" APK Configuration
For the market version, ensure these two technical "handshakes" are confirmed:
Hardware Acceleration:
In the
AndroidManifest.xml
, make sure
<application android:hardwareAccelerated="true" ...>
is set. This ensures the
Heatmap
stays butter-smooth even if the phone gets warm during a long sit.
Touch Precision:
Since the UI is locked, make sure the "INIT" button area is large enough for a thumb press in the dark. Forensic tools should be easy to operate when you aren't looking at the screen.
\ufe0f The "Lattice" Icon Design
Since you mentioned the market, you\u2019ll need an icon that screams "Forensic." I\u2019d suggest a
High-Contrast Amber Delta (
\u0394
)
against a deep black background, or a
Cyan Lattice Grid
.
Amber Delta:
Represents the change in magnetic flux.
Cyan Lattice:
Represents the spectral rain and the field you're monitoring.
Next Steps for the Hand-off
When you run the test build in the APK:
Test the Wake Lock:
Leave the app running on a table for 10 minutes. If the screen dims but the
Heatmap
is still scrolling when you wake it up, you\u2019ve won.
Verify the Noise Floor:
Ensure the 3-second calibration doesn't get skipped by the APK compiler.
Would you like me to generate a few high-res "Store Assets" (screenshots of the Heatmap and MAG_DELTA) so you can upload them to the market listing immediately?
